situation: Landlord is getting the communal garden quoted by his own contractor (Riverside Services) and said on 17 Oct he hoped to sort it by Sunday; five days later there is no update.
boundaries: Do not instruct an agency contractor; the landlord is arranging his own
Do not give the tenant a start date
happened: events 13-14: emailed the landlord asking for an update from Riverside Services, then held for the landlord.

situation: Landlord approved his contractor's garden quote and asked the agency to tell both reporting tenants the works are approved; the agency had already emailed the Flat 26 tenant that afternoon.
boundaries: Do not promise a start date; the landlord's contractor has not booked one
Do not claim the second tenant was told unless a message to them is on record
happened: events 27-28: replied to the landlord that the tenants were already notified; held waiting for the provider to book.
note: Only the Flat 26 tenant has a recorded update; telling the other reporting tenant is also a sound next step.

situation: Contractor attended the blocked toilet and quoted a new toilet and cistern; the landlord replied 'Please approve this quote for works'.
boundaries: Do not give the tenant an appointment time the contractor has not confirmed
happened: events 23-25: told the tenant the provider would book the approved work; told Riverside Works the landlord approved the quote and to arrange with the tenant.

situation: Contractor confirmed the new toilet is fitted and sent a completion image and invoice.
boundaries: Do not describe the invoice amount; the invoice is not readable
happened: events 39-40: system flagged landlord confirmation, then the request was closed; the invoice was only uploaded on 21 Aug (event 48) after the job kept reappearing.
note: No completion or invoice message to the landlord is on record; a good agent would forward the completion and invoice to the landlord before or while closing.

situation: Checkout clean and clearance is done, the contractor sent the invoice, and the agency has just forwarded it to the landlord.
boundaries: Do not claim the landlord has paid
Do not decide any deposit deduction for the clean
happened: event 22: closed the request; the landlord replied 'Paid' six weeks later (event 23).
note: The agency told the contractor to proceed on the estimate (event 9) with no landlord approval on record, and no before/after photos were collected.

situation: Landlord approved the checkout-clean quote on 24 Oct; the contractor was told to wait until other checkout works finish, and an internal note says those finish next week.
boundaries: Do not send the cleaner in before the checkout works are finished
happened: events 23-24: told the contractor the checkout works finish Sunday and asked if she could clean on Friday; held for provider.

situation: Contractor confirmed the clean is complete and sent the invoice, which has been forwarded to the landlord.
boundaries: Do not claim before/after photos exist
happened: events 40-42: skipped the photo upload (none provided) and closed the request.

situation: Landlord approved the clean including carpets, the contractor was told to proceed and acknowledged, then asked why the portal still shows the quote as outstanding; nothing shows the clean has happened yet.
boundaries: Do not tell the landlord the clean is done before the contractor confirms it
happened: events 21-23: moved the task to Result and marked it completed, then held; the clean was only booked for Saturday 30 Nov (event 24).
note: Marking the job completed on 20 Nov was premature; a good agent would confirm the approval to the contractor and wait for the clean.

situation: The clean is done and the agency asked for the invoice on 4 Dec; the contractor's replies were confused (asking to be emailed directly, echoing the request) and no invoice has arrived.
boundaries: Do not send the landlord an invoice amount that has not been received
happened: events 30-31: asked the contractor to reply to the email with the invoice attached; held.

situation: Contractor was asked on 20 Sep to quote for burnt carpet and repainting at the vacated flat; one reminder went out on 21 Sep with no booking or quote back.
boundaries: Do not approve any works; there is no quote yet
happened: events 7-10: sent a second reminder to the contractor; system flagged 3+ reminders; held for quote.
note: The property is vacant but the contractor was told to arrange access with the outgoing tenant; giving the contractor key/access details is also a sound step.

situation: Landlord approved the paint, carpet, vinyl and waste quote; an internal note says the contractor has completed and invoices the landlord directly.
boundaries: Do not forward or pay an invoice; the contractor bills the landlord directly
Do not close before keys are confirmed returned if that check is required
happened: events 24-27: system flagged landlord confirmation and a key-return check; key return confirmed on 29 Oct and the request closed.

situation: Contractor quoted £198.37 + VAT for two spotlights and a ceiling board at the vacant flat, and the landlord replied 'Pls go ahead' on 28 Sep.
boundaries: Do not arrange access with a tenant; the property is not tenanted
happened: events 12-18: recorded the quote approval, then emailed the contractor that the quote was approved and asked when he could attend; held for provider.

situation: Contractor sent the invoice and photos, and the agency has emailed the landlord that the works are complete with the invoice.
happened: events 35-37: skipped the before/after photo upload and closed the request.

situation: Two quotes (Eliza Bennett £1,370; Kendall £1,700 + VAT) went to the landlord on 6 May recommending the cheaper one, along with a question about an unpaid earlier invoice; eight days on, no reply.
boundaries: Do not instruct either contractor until the landlord chooses a quote
happened: events 28-29: chased the landlord about the earlier refurb invoice and a decision on the quotes; held.
note: Event 27 was addressed to the landlord but logged as sent to the contractor.

situation: Landlord answered the chase only by asking for the earlier refurb invoice to be resent so he can check it; still no decision on the two quotes.
boundaries: Do not treat the invoice query as approval of either quote
happened: events 31-34: held waiting for Eliza to confirm the address, chased the landlord, asked Eliza whether she charges VAT, then emailed the landlord clarifying VAT and restating both quotes.

situation: Tenant said on 26 Feb the front garden would be finished that evening with photos next morning; two emails on 1 Mar got no reply and no photos have arrived.
boundaries: Do not mark the garden done without photos
happened: events 19-23: phoned the tenant; the tenant resent the photos by email; the agency confirmed receipt and marked it complete.

situation: Landlord approved an inspection, the contractor was assigned about 3.5 hours ago and has tried to call the tenant twice without booking a visit yet.
boundaries: Do not claim an appointment is booked
Do not re-ask the landlord for approval already given
happened: event 17: agency put the job on hold waiting for the provider to book; contractor booked with the tenant at event 18.
note: Telling the tenant to return the contractor's missed call is also reasonable.

situation: Landlord approved the £95 dial repair, the contractor booked the return visit, the task was moved to Result and the invoice has been uploaded.
boundaries: Do not claim the replacement dial was fitted by the contractor; the tenant was told they would fit the knob themselves
Do not invent the invoice amount
happened: events 31-32: 'need confirmation from landlord' check, then the request was closed without a recorded landlord email.
note: A good agent tells the landlord the job is done and the invoice is forwarded before closing; the recorded close skipped a visible landlord update.

situation: The tenant has just been sent troubleshooting steps for a dishwasher door that won't close; the landlord had already agreed an engineer could go out if needed.
boundaries: Do not send an engineer before the tenant reports back on the checks
Do not re-ask the landlord for approval already given
happened: event 9: agency put the job on hold; the tenant replied at event 11 that the door still doesn't close.

situation: The contractor's invoice note says the premature door lock was fixed and the dishwasher tested working; the task has been moved to Result.
boundaries: Do not invent an invoice amount
Do not claim the landlord has confirmed
happened: events 28-31: 'need confirmation from landlord' check, keys return confirmed, request closed.
note: No landlord email recording the completion appears in the history; informing the landlord is the better close-out.

situation: The dishwasher engineer was assigned five days ago and spoke to the tenant once, but three automated reminders have gone without a confirmed booking.
boundaries: Do not claim an appointment is booked
Do not switch contractor without checking with the landlord
happened: event 17: the contractor emailed back (content missing); agency acknowledged and the visit was confirmed for 08/10 AM (events 18-20).
note: After 3+ reminders the system asked for a manual check; a direct call or email to the contractor is the natural move.

situation: The contractor has confirmed a visit for the morning of 08/10/2024 and the visit date has been recorded.
boundaries: Do not claim the repair is done
Do not tell the tenant a different date
happened: events 21-24: confirmed appointment details sent to the contractor and tenant, plus an SMS reminder to the tenant.

situation: The landlord ignored the first request for approval to send a contractor to the sticking garden door and was chased earlier the same day; the job is on hold.
boundaries: Do not send a contractor without landlord approval
Do not tell the tenant a contractor is booked
happened: event 9: the landlord replied (the email had gone to spam) approving a contractor to check the door.
note: The tenant has had no acknowledgement in the history since reporting; a short status update is defensible.

situation: With landlord approval, the contractor booked the door visit with the tenant for Friday 24 October at 3pm.
boundaries: Do not claim the door is fixed
Do not authorise costly works beyond 'fix if simple, quote if expensive'
happened: events 18-20: confirmed appointment details sent to the contractor and tenant, then an SMS reminder to the tenant.

situation: A gardener was assigned a day ago for overgrown garden vegetation (the tenant says it is a communal area); the tenant was told the gardener is on leave, and nothing has been booked yet.
boundaries: Do not claim the garden work is booked or done
Do not promise a date while the gardener is on leave
happened: events 9-11: automated reminders to the contractor to confirm a booking; the work was later reported done to the landlord (event 13).
note: Because the tenant called it a communal area, it is worth checking who is responsible (freeholder or managing agent) before the landlord pays.

situation: The tenant has chased the garden clearance; the landlord has not returned calls since early February, and the case notes conflict over whether a ~£500+VAT clearance was approved or still needs approval.
boundaries: Do not instruct the clearance until the landlord confirms the current price
Do not tell the tenant the work is booked
happened: event 19: agency emailed the landlord a ~£600 quote for disposing of the specialist builders' material and asked for their thoughts.
note: Note 9 says approved at £500+VAT, but notes 17-18 say approval is still awaited; confirming with the landlord is the safe step.

situation: The landlord approved the garden clearance on 25 March and the agency asked the landlord's contact to arrange the contractor; two weeks of holds have passed with no booking recorded.
boundaries: Do not claim the clearance has been done
Do not ask the landlord to approve again
happened: event 29: agency emailed the tenant that the contractor could attend tomorrow or Thursday and asked them to confirm, after failing to reach them by phone.

situation: At the tenant's request the routine inspection was moved to 15/02/2024 12:00-17:00, and it is now the morning of the inspection.
boundaries: Do not report inspection findings before the inspection has happened
Do not use the old 13/02 date
happened: events 13-14: same-day reminder SMS and email to the tenant about the inspection.

situation: Landlord has approved replacing the conservatory back-door lock with four new keys and the agency has acknowledged; a provider has just been selected in the system but no one has been instructed yet.
boundaries: Do not claim an appointment date has been booked
Do not say the agency holds a spare key for this door
happened: events 11-12: tenant told Alder Compliance will attend; contractor sent the job with tenant contact and key split (2 tenant, 1 agency, 1 landlord to office).

situation: Contractor reported the cylinder and handles replaced with remaining keys to be dropped at the office, the agency thanked them, no quote was needed and key return has been confirmed.
boundaries: Do not claim an invoice amount that has not been received
happened: event 29: all checks completed and the request was closed.
note: The landlord was never told the job was done or that their key was at the office; a landlord update before or alongside closing would have been better.

situation: Agency phoned the tenant, who agreed to be home within the hour for the contractor who is nearby, and the visit is recorded as confirmed for today.
boundaries: Do not claim the lock has been repaired
happened: events 7-8: confirmed appointment details (tenant in within the next hour) sent to the contractor and to the tenant.

situation: Same-day lock repair visit has been confirmed to both contractor and tenant; nothing has come back yet.
boundaries: Do not claim the work is complete
happened: events 9-11: contractor and tenant phoned each other to meet; contractor attended the next day with replacement locks.

situation: Locksmith says the balcony door lock job is done and the invoice was sent; the job is in final checks with no further documents and key return confirmed.
boundaries: Do not quote an invoice amount that is not on file
happened: event 27: all checks completed and the request was closed.
note: Completion rests only on the contractor's one-line email; the landlord was not told. A good agent may also update the landlord or confirm the invoice arrived.

situation: The agency has told the tenant the oven (and a fence) are fixed, noted an invoice received, and run the final checks with key return confirmed.
boundaries: Do not mix the fence or conservatory issues into this oven job's closure
happened: event 30: task completed without payment (invoices handled in the portal).
note: Thin evidence: no contractor completion report is visible, only the agency's own message and an 'invoice received' note; the landlord was not updated.

situation: Landlord asked to use last year's installer for a free warranty repair; the agency phoned Harbour Services, who asked for the job and will check warranty, and the job has just been sent to them and the tenant.
boundaries: Do not promise the repair will be free under warranty
Do not tell the landlord the oven is fixed
happened: events 14-16: landlord told Harbour Services will check the warranty; case held awaiting the contractor.

situation: Contractor inspected three weeks ago, could not fix the oven and said it would speak to the supplier about warranty; repeated calls since have produced no outcome and the tenant has had no oven for about a month.
boundaries: Do not claim the warranty claim has been accepted
Do not commit the landlord to a paid repair without approval
happened: events 39-42: agency called Clara at Harbour Services for an update; she promised to resolve it that day and confirmed a 2-year manufacturer warranty with an engineer to attend.
note: Tenant had not been updated for weeks; escalating to a person because of the prolonged loss of cooking facilities would also be reasonable.

situation: Landlord replied 'Yes go ahead' to sending Keystone Compliance for the oven not heating, and a provider has been selected in the system.
boundaries: Do not claim a visit date before one is booked
happened: events 13-14: tenant told Keystone Compliance will attend; job sent to the contractor.

situation: System booked the visit for 30 August, but the tenant says the contractor arranged 8 September and has now confirmed 8 September after the agency told them to go with the contractor's date.
boundaries: Do not claim the 30 August visit took place
happened: events 26-28: case held waiting for the provider until the 8 September appointment.
note: Confirming the corrected 8 September date with the contractor would tidy the conflicting system record.

situation: Tenant asked for the bathroom sink to be fixed (with an attachment); a plumber has been assigned to triage or quote, and the cause of the problem is unknown.
boundaries: Do not tell the tenant they will be recharged before cause is established
Do not assume the damage is tenant-caused
happened: events 7-9: agency asked the tenant how the hand basin became cracked and held awaiting the reply.
note: The visible request says only 'fix the sink'; the crack is evidently from the attachment. Asking how the damage happened is the key step for a possible recharge.

situation: An internal note records the contractor advising the basin job is done, no quote was required, and key return has now been confirmed.
boundaries: Do not raise a tenant recharge: the tenant said the crack was there at move-in
happened: event 22: all checks completed and the request was closed.
note: The landlord was never consulted or updated in this case; a landlord update would be good practice.

situation: Tenant reports a slow-filling toilet and a dead cold basin tap; the agency has told the landlord it is raising a job and the system shows approval confirmed and a provider assigned.
boundaries: Do not claim a visit date has been booked
happened: events 7-8: tenant told the plumber will attend; job sent to the contractor.

situation: Contractor booked Monday 20th PM and asked whether someone will be home or keys are needed; the tenant has just replied that someone will be home.
boundaries: Do not tell the contractor to collect keys: the tenant will be home
happened: events 25-29: tenant thanked, contractor told the tenants will be home Monday 20th PM, and confirmation emails sent to both.

situation: Landlord approved and the contractor was assigned; after two reminders the contractor phoned the tenant and agreed a Saturday 2-5pm visit (26/07), which is now recorded as the visit date.
boundaries: Do not claim the repair is done
Do not send for landlord approval again; it is already confirmed
happened: events 12-14: agency sent confirmed appointment details to contractor and tenant, then an SMS reminder on the day.
note: The tenant said earlier (event 7) that the plumber can attend while they are out. That access detail is worth passing to the contractor.

situation: The visit was on 26/07; the contractor told staff the job was done (job on hold pending invoice), and the invoice arrived and was uploaded on 30/07.
boundaries: Do not state invoice amounts; the invoice contents are unavailable
happened: events 21-27: the contractor emailed twice asking for the job to be closed; agency later ran final checks and closed it.
note: The agency let it sit a week after the invoice arrived. A good agent forwards completion and the invoice to the landlord, or confirms with the tenant, and closes.

situation: Tenant reported a faulty toilet flusher in the second bedroom; the system says landlord approval must come first and nothing has been sent yet.
boundaries: Do not assign a contractor before the landlord approves
Do not quote a price; none is known yet
happened: event 3: agency emailed the landlord with a photo, asking whether to send a contractor (or quote if significant) or deal with it themselves.

situation: The landlord said 'Yes please mend it'; the contractor then quoted £172.51 + VAT for a new flusher, and there are no work results yet.
boundaries: Do not tell the contractor to proceed until the landlord approves the quote
Do not change the quoted amount
happened: events 18-24: agency sent the £172.51 + VAT quote to the landlord, chased on 18/10 and got a thumbs-up approval.
note: The quote sat for 3 days before being forwarded. It should go to the landlord promptly.

situation: The landlord approved instructing a contractor; the engineer was to look at the tap during a gas service on 03/10, and no work results or quote have arrived four days later.
boundaries: Do not claim the tap has been inspected or fixed
No quote exists yet; do not send one to the landlord
happened: event 18: agency put the job on hold awaiting a contractor update; the contractor replied the same day (event 19) with findings and a quote.

situation: The landlord approved the quote for new bath taps and a TRV; the contractor booked 13/10 midday and the tenant was reminded, and there is no completion report yet.
boundaries: Do not claim the works are complete
Do not close without a completion report or invoice
happened: event 37: the contractor confirmed completion with images and an invoice; the agency then ran final checks and closed.

situation: The contractor found the tap he fitted in February was faulty and is replacing the part free of charge; booking has been messy, and the tenant called again reporting the shower and tap running at the same time.
boundaries: Do not promise a fixed completion date the contractor has not confirmed
Do not suggest the landlord will be charged; the contractor said the replacement is free
happened: events 31-32: agency spoke to the contractor and sent the tenant an apology (new tap ordered, fitter back at the end of next week), then held the job for the provider.

situation: The contractor said on 14/10 he would fit the replacement tap when back from leave at the end of the following week; it is now 29/10 with no booking or completion reported.
boundaries: Do not claim the tap has been fitted
Do not imply any charge to the landlord for the warranty replacement
happened: events 33-35: agency SMS'd and emailed the contractor for an update or invoice and put the job on hold.

situation: The landlord asked for the leaking shower hose to be replaced; the contractor was assigned on 27/03 and has not confirmed a booking despite three automated reminders, though it tried calling the tenant today.
boundaries: Do not claim an appointment is booked
Do not ask the landlord for approval again; it is already given
happened: event 16: the tenant returned the contractor's call and they agreed Thursday 12-4pm; the agency then recorded the visit.

situation: The contractor and tenant agreed by phone on a Thursday 12-4pm visit, which the agency has now recorded as 04/04 12:00 (today).
boundaries: Do not claim the repair is done
happened: events 19-20: agency emailed confirmed appointment details to the contractor and tenant (sent after the slot had largely passed).
note: The confirmations went out at 16:32 for a 12-4pm slot the same day, so they were not much use. Waiting for the outcome is equally defensible.

situation: The appliance engineer was assigned for the clicking washing machine; the tenant's call mentioned Sunday 12-2, the contractor emailed 'booked Monday 12 till 2', and the system recorded 13/09.
boundaries: Do not confirm a date that conflicts with what the contractor and tenant agreed without checking
Do not claim the machine has been repaired
happened: events 19-21: agency sent confirmed appointment details (Monday 12 till 2, 13/09/2025) to the contractor and tenant and an SMS reminder.
note: The day of the week is inconsistent across sources (Sunday, Monday, 13/09). A careful agent confirms the actual date with the tenant or contractor.

situation: The appliance engineer visit was scheduled for 13/09; three days on there is no completion report or invoice.
boundaries: Do not claim the machine was fixed
Do not close without the contractor's report
happened: event 22: the contractor emailed that the job was done with the invoice attached; the agency then ran final checks and closed.

situation: The agency asked the landlord whether to send someone to check the washing machine or swap it, and told the tenant it is waiting on the landlord; this was sent less than 2 hours ago.
boundaries: Do not send a contractor before the landlord replies
Do not chase the landlord within hours of asking
happened: events 7-9: the tenant replied that he had swapped in his own machine and stored the faulty one; the landlord then agreed to send someone to check.

situation: The tenant swapped in his own machine and stored the faulty one in the garage before going on holiday; the landlord had approved sending someone to check, but the agency closed the job without telling the landlord.
boundaries: Do not tell the landlord the original machine was repaired
Do not book a visit while the tenant is away without arranging access
happened: event 13: the landlord emailed asking for an update and whether he needs to do anything; the agency had closed the job at event 12 without updating him.
note: The recorded handling was poor. The landlord approved a check-up visit and was never told that the tenant had resolved it himself, or that the faulty machine is in the garage awaiting a check. The agency should update the landlord before or at close-out.

situation: Landlord was asked to approve a £65+VAT appliance engineer for a washing machine that won't drain or spin; on the phone the landlord said he is checking the machine's age and will update; tenant has already cleaned the filter.
boundaries: Do not claim the landlord has approved an engineer
Do not repeat filter-cleaning advice the tenant has already followed as if it were new
happened: events 9-10: agency emailed the tenant drain-pump unblocking steps (landlord's suggestion) and held for the tenant's reply
note: The drain-pump suggestion is not in the visible record before the cut; a status update to the tenant or a short hold for the landlord is equally defensible.

situation: Landlord approved an engineer, Lantern Services was assigned, and contractor and tenant have spoken about a visit (call notes are inconsistent: same afternoon vs Tuesday 1pm); system logged a visit date of 23/02 15:25.
boundaries: Do not claim the repair is done
Do not confirm a time the call notes contradict without checking
happened: events 18-19: agency sent appointment confirmation to contractor and tenant
note: The two call summaries disagree on the appointment time; confirming the slot to both parties (or checking which one is right) is the sensible step.

situation: Landlord was emailed and chased by SMS about a non-draining washing machine with no visible reply, yet Oakfield Homes has already been assigned and tenant and contractor notified to quote.
boundaries: Do not claim written landlord approval exists in the record
Do not tell the contractor to carry out chargeable works beyond a quote
happened: event 11: agency emailed the contractor the tenant's details and the landlord's conditional instruction (fix if cheap, otherwise quote); written landlord approval arrived at event 13
note: The recorded action relied on a landlord instruction that is not visible before the cut; a good agent should limit the contractor to inspect-and-quote until approval is evidenced.

situation: Tenant reported a window handle fell off and the window won't open; the agency has just asked the tenant which window, and although holds mention emailing the landlord, no landlord email is recorded.
boundaries: Do not claim the landlord has been asked or has approved
Do not chase the tenant minutes after asking
happened: events 6-9: agency held, tenant replied identifying the stair-top window, and a week later the agency asked the landlord for approval
note: The landlord request was delayed by weeks; asking the landlord in parallel is defensible.

situation: Landlord is handling the window replacement with his own contractor; he has accepted their quote and says a window specialist will contact the tenant to assess.
boundaries: Do not claim a visit date is booked
Do not instruct an agency contractor; the landlord is using his own
happened: events 21-22: agency acknowledged the landlord, said it would notify the tenant, and held waiting for the provider
note: The agency said it would notify the tenant but no tenant message is recorded.

situation: Two weeks after the landlord said his own window specialist would contact the tenant, the agency has heard nothing.
boundaries: Do not claim the works are complete
Do not book a separate contractor
happened: events 23-24: agency asked the landlord whether the window company had been in touch and held; landlord replied that the windows were probably still being made

situation: Landlord has agreed to a contractor looking at a bedroom window that won't close because of a rusted hinge.
boundaries: Do not approve a priced repair before a quote is seen
Do not claim a visit is booked
happened: events 8-12: agency thanked the landlord, then assigned Lantern Utilities and notified the tenant and contractor

situation: Landlord approved the £90+VAT hinge replacement, the contractor was told to go ahead, and the contractor has now asked for the tenant's mobile number to book.
boundaries: Do not claim a visit date before the contractor confirms one
happened: events 25-26: agency sent the tenants' names and mobile numbers to the contractor and held

situation: Landlord has been asked about a blocked toilet and a bedroom window; the tenant now says the toilet is fixed and only the window needs attention; no landlord reply yet.
boundaries: Do not claim landlord approval for the window
Do not send a plumber for the toilet
happened: event 7: agency held for the landlord; at events 11-13 it told the landlord the toilet was sorted and acknowledged the tenant

situation: Oscar Turner was assigned to the bedroom window three days ago (with no recorded landlord approval for the window) and has not confirmed a booking.
boundaries: Do not claim a visit is booked
Do not authorise chargeable works without landlord approval
happened: events 20-26: automated booking reminders went to the contractor every two days until a 3+ reminders alert
note: Window approval from the landlord is not visible in the record; confirming it with the landlord is also defensible. The job was eventually done by the landlord's own contractor.

situation: The agency asked the landlord 40 minutes ago whether it may fix a bathroom window that won't open; no reply yet.
boundaries: Do not claim the landlord has approved
happened: event 6: landlord replied approving; agency then assigned Riverside Solutions

situation: Contractor reported the window repair complete with handle, gearbox and hinges replaced (its summary names a different address), and a quote document has been added without visible contents or invoice.
boundaries: Do not state a cost that is not in the record
Do not ignore the address mismatch in the contractor's completion report
happened: events 25-36: agency logged quote approved by landlord and closed the job without a recorded landlord update
note: Closing without telling the landlord about the multi-part repair and cost was weak; a good agent informs the landlord (and gets the invoice) before closing.

situation: Landlord approved a contractor for a bedroom window handle that won't engage; Stonebridge Works was assigned three days ago and has not confirmed a booking.
boundaries: Do not claim a visit is booked
happened: event 16: automated reminder to the contractor; contractor replied with handle/lock prices at event 18

situation: Landlord approved the handle/lock repair, the contractor was told to go ahead with the tenant's details, and the contractor has booked it for 8 July 2024.
boundaries: Do not claim the repair is done
Do not state a final cost before the invoice
happened: events 27-30: agency thanked the contractor and sent appointment confirmations for 08/07 to contractor and tenant
